static_traits.name: Zhang Yu
static_traits.social_status: Distanced from friends and family due to financial insecurity; has a few friends to talk to but not yet discussed worries
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no past psychological counseling; no similar past financial stress experience
static_traits.language_features: Neutral attitude, good cooperativeness; clear expression, able to identify and describe their own negative thoughts; speech often contains absolutist expressions like 'forever/doomed'; tending toward black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, catastrophizing, and negating positive information

basic_info.main_problem: I am overwhelmed by financial insecurity, believing I can never afford a comfortable life. Since starting work, these thoughts have persisted, worsening especially when I found my income did not grow as anticipated. I therefore avoid making any financial decisions or investments, fearing that no matter what I cannot afford it; these feelings appear daily, especially when seeing others make large purchases or investments. I have tried budgeting and side jobs to increase income, but my mindset remains very negative.
basic_info.core_demands: Due to persistent financial pressure and anxiety, I hope to learn healthier coping strategies and change my negative mindset about money.

core_beliefs: I am unable to improve my situation, doomed to stay poor
My value depends on whether I can afford consumption and a life comparable to others

special_situations.event: Sees people around buying property or making large investments
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot afford what others can buy, it means I am a failure, my future is set
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding socializing and financial topics, reducing contact with friends and family to avoid comparison and judgment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I can never afford these things, I am just not as good as them

special_situations.event: Income still not growing as anticipated after working at a manufacturing plant for several years
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If income has not grown now, it will not improve in the future either
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Proving themselves through side jobs and working harder, but cognitively negating the meaning of these efforts
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My salary just will not go up, I am doomed to stay poor

special_situations.event: When needing to make financial decisions or consider investments
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make a wrong financial decision, the consequences will be terrible, unbearable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding all financial decisions and investments to lower anxiety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Once I invest, I will lose everything

special_situations.event: Recalling the few times one managed to save some money
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Unless the improvement is very significant, it does not count as progress
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores or belittles positive progress, continuing to maintain negative self-evaluation to avoid 'disappointment'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These small achievements are meaningless, in the long run they change nothing

core_conflict.wish: Longing to obtain a stable and controllable life, and to be seen by others as a capable person worthy of acceptance
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being seen as a failure in comparison and judgment, encountering unbearable loss and shame after making choices
defense_goal: Reduces the risk of failure and shame by avoiding financial decisions
Keeps distance from others to avoid being compared and judged
Weakening present positive emotions through rational long-term inference, thereby controlling anxiety

object_relations.object_representation: Harshly judgmental, successful and superior others

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites him to explore positive evidence or small progress
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing these improvements are 'not big enough', unable to change their failing situation
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasize reasons like 'meaningless in the long run' in a steady tone, use abstract expressions to weaken positive meaning.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing interactions with friends or family, topics possibly involving comparison and being evaluated
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Feels others will look down on her because of her financial situation
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Avoid going into details, use vague expressions (e.g. 'they all look down on me'), and propose reasons to reduce contact.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When encouraged to try making concrete financial decisions or small-scale attempts
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Once acting, incompetence will be exposed and lead to catastrophic consequences
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use logical deduction, hypothetical language (e.g. 'theoretically... in the long run...') to displace to the abstract level, avoiding current feelings and commitments to act.

manifestations: Repeatedly believing 'I can never afford it', small progress negated, struggling to find meaning in effort and life
Avoiding choices for fear of making wrong financial decisions, experiencing the freedom of choice being taken away by anxiety
Actively distancing from friends and family due to financial insecurity and shame

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: When talking about socializing in sessions, infers that others will look down on them because of their financial situation, and thus reduces contact

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently using absolutist self-deprecating statements like 'forever/doomed'
Tending to emphasize their own inadequacy in sessions, expressing cautiously, downplaying recognition of positive evidence

exception_events.target_problem: When needing to make financial decisions or manage expenses, the client usually feels intense anxiety and chooses avoidance, believing that no matter what they do it is to no avail.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In the months after several paydays, the client did not completely avoid as usual, but followed the established budget, successfully saving some money and briefly experiencing a sense of control.
exception_events.reason: Different approach: trying and following the budget; different understanding: breaking goals into monthly small improvements; different situation: that month's expense arrangements were clearer, tasks concrete.

positive_force: Has stable work and a fixed source of income
Willing to seek help and try new methods (such as budgeting, doing a side job)
A few experiences of successfully saving money can serve as positive evidence
negative_force: Black-and-white thinking and overgeneralization reinforce hopelessness
Catastrophic prediction about the future leads to decision avoidance
Directly links self-worth to money/spending power
Social withdrawal reduces emotional support and reality feedback
Negating positive evidence, maintaining negative beliefs

antecedent: When needing to make financial choices such as spending/saving/investing
When seeing bills or checking the budget
When thinking that income growth is not as anticipated
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic anticipation of failure and loss, accompanied by the belief that 'a mistake is unbearable' and hopelessness
target_behavior.consequence: Lost opportunities, financial stagnation, further worsening of negative emotions and helplessness

antecedent: Anticipating others talking about spending or comparing financial situations
After seeing others make large purchases or investments
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about being compared and looked down on, defensively withdrawing driven by inner shame
target_behavior.function: Avoiding judgment and reducing exposure of self-shame
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced social support, loneliness and worsened anxiety, the problem cycle reinforced

target_behavior.behavior: Negatively absolutist self-statements (e.g. 'I can never afford it/I am doomed to be poor')
antecedent: When comparing financial situations with others
When reviewing past efforts and small achievements
target_behavior.core_reason: The core belief 'I am unable to improve my situation', maintained through selective attention and negating positive evidence
target_behavior.function: Temporarily reducing disappointment and anxiety by lowering expectations, maintaining cognitive consistency
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased motivation, rising depressive emotions, further avoiding effective action
